summary: EU region: customers reporting pinned model responses coming from fallback variant
related_confluence_pages: Postmortem: INC-2025-1012 Unintended model fallback in eu-west (quality regression)
description:
Customer reports that despite strict model pinning, responses intermittently include a different model identifier and output quality changes. Customer also saw slightly higher latency and more formatting errors.

Impact:
- Production customer traffic in eu-west
- Customer-visible correctness regression

What we need:
- Confirm whether router policy is selecting fallback unexpectedly
- Confirm if this is limited to eu-west

Customer evidence:
- Request IDs shared via Support portal (see comments)
comments: 2025-10-12 Chloe Martin (Support): Customer (Acme Analytics) says pinned model changed mid-day. They noticed response header model=rw-qwen2.5-72b-int4 even though they pinned rw-llama-3.1-70b-2025-09-30. They also mention a change in refusal behavior.
2025-10-12 Ethan Park (Eng): Looking at eu-west routing metrics now. Seeing route_fallback_selected spikes that do not correlate with GPU saturation. Pulling router policy diff deployed this morning.
2025-10-12 Monica Patel (SRE): Incident declared as INC-2025-1012. Likely policy-induced fallback. Rolling back routing config and flushing policy cache.
2025-10-12 Chloe Martin (Support): Customer shared sample request ids: 9f12c2e0-..., 3ab88d9d-..., 7c0c9a1b-... They confirm time window ~09:20-10:50 UTC.

2025-10-13 Ethan Park (Eng): Root cause: router treated transient queue depth spikes as sustained overload and marked fallback eligible. Fix: rollback + add guardrail for strict pinning when primary healthy.
2025-10-14 Chloe Martin (Support): Confirmed with customer: model id stable again and quality is back to expected. Closing ticket; linking to postmortem once published.
